title: Control symbol-outline cost by language, kind, depth, and location

state.decision_rationale: Accepted as useful/full/none symbol policies with per-language depth and location filtering plus total/emitted counts.

provenance.source_label: Claude Fable critique 1: symbols are the worst cost center
provenance.review_target: Reported 39479-line MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: The symbols section is 362 KB of a 1.62 MB packet. Gate outline generation by language, kind, or depth, drop unlocatable entries, or make symbol depth a projection knob such as exports-only, top-level, or full.
feedback.normalized_claim: Symbol outlines need an explicit usefulness and budget policy so low-value config keys, deep entries, and unlocatable records do not consume a disproportionate share of context.

current_behavior: The packet emits every symbol returned by the analyzer, including nested structured-data keys, with depth, name, kind, range posture, exported posture, and optional signature.
There is no per-language, per-kind, per-depth, exports-only, top-level-only, or budget-aware outline filter.
Symbols with unavailable ranges remain present as range=unknown, preserving analyzer knowledge but weakening citation value.
The reviewer's packet-specific 362 KB, 2681-entry, and 489-unknown measurements are reported provenance rather than reproduced repository evidence.

proposal.summary: Benchmark and define configurable symbol projections that retain the most task-useful structural navigation per token while reporting what was filtered.
candidate_changes: Add named symbol projection levels such as none, exports-only, top-level, located, and full.
Allow deterministic language, kind, and depth policies with explicit packet metadata and omission counts.
Evaluate whether unlocatable symbols should be removed, summarized, or retained only in full mode.
Measure symbol-section tokens and task accuracy by language and projection level.
non_goals: Do not silently discard analyzer results while still claiming a full outline.
Do not assume all range=unknown symbols are useless without task evaluation.
Do not encode programming-language export semantics onto config keys without a declared meaning.

questions: Which symbol kinds measurably help code navigation, retrieval, and review?
Should config and documentation outlines use separate structural vocabularies?
How are filtered symbol counts and reasons represented without recreating the same overhead?
risks: Aggressive filtering can remove the exact nested key or private symbol needed for a task.
Language-specific policies can fragment packet behavior.
Projection knobs can complicate identity and cross-packet comparisons.
evidence_needed: Reproduction of the reported section-size and range-availability measurements.
Per-language ablation studies on symbol-assisted model tasks.
Token and retrieval comparisons for candidate outline levels.
